title: Native system-transaction accounting and proposal validation
condition: Native system-transaction execution and subsequent fee/refund accounting do not maintain one consistent funding rule. Proposal validation does not establish a sufficiently narrow admissible system-transaction set or an explicit deterministic base-fee equality check.
impact: A proposer-controlled block path is the relevant prerequisite. If reachable in installed consensus participants, unfunded native credits threaten supply integrity and the economic backing of native bridge assets. This is separate from external RPC evidence trust.
evidence: Frozen node state/executor.go, types/transaction.go, consensus/ibft/fork/hooks.go and block/header validation were traced. Completed isolated accounting checks observed unfunded credits, including the real ProcessBlock path. Confidential evidence retains the local outputs; no full malicious consensus proposal was constructed or broadcast.
remediation: Constrain system transactions at block validation, make non-fee-bearing semantics consistent through execution, verify deterministic header fees, and add supply-conservation/rejection regressions. Publish a corrected release and attest every installed validator binary before approval.
limits: The automated security filter stopped deeper exploit-oriented reproduction. Installed-node exposure and complete end-to-end consensus acceptance are not established. Existing Interchain tests passing does not resolve this accounting boundary.

title: Transaction-original storage and refund accounting
condition: The transaction-original storage baseline is not consistently replaced between transactions, while refund subtraction permits unsigned underflow.
impact: Multiple storage updates across transactions can be charged or refunded incorrectly. The execution refund cap limits the demonstrated effect; this issue alone does not establish unlimited refunds or arbitrary minting.
evidence: Node state/txn.go:221-287,449-457,480-488,550-584 and state/executor.go:479-483. A completed isolated refund-state check observed wrapping; full multi-transaction network reproduction was not performed.
remediation: Maintain transaction-local original-slot state, enforce refund arithmetic invariants and verify cross-transaction storage-gas cases under the correct fork rules. Coordinate any consensus-semantic correction.
limits: Source tracing and a local arithmetic check support the finding; no live exploit or complete EVM transaction sequence was verified.

title: Expensive gossip work lacks complete admission bounds
condition: Checkpoint-vote and quorum-hint messages can reach full source verification before adequate member/signature admission and global bounded concurrency control. Governance-proposal admission also lacks global count, disk and maximum-future-lease bounds.
impact: Adversarial peer traffic can consume RPC, CPU and worker capacity shared with the validator process. Optional-worker separation from synchronous IBFT hooks does not prove host resource isolation.
evidence: Node interchain/runtime/worker.go:830-880, iln_checkpoint.go:168-201, iln_quorum_request.go:211-238, governance.go:201-240 and network/gossip.go:108-122; bounded local seam observation and standard/race tests.
remediation: Add cheap admissibility checks, per-peer and global limits, bounded concurrency, in-flight deduplication and fair service before remote reads. Bound accepted governance count, disk use and maximum future lease. Preserve complete source verification before signing; demonstrate consensus continuity under controlled load.
limits: No production flood or demonstrated IBFT outage. Transport deadlines and existing selected-message throttles mitigate individual requests.

title: Shared observer retry fairness and failure isolation
condition: Durable retries improve poisoned-operation isolation, but a fixed route iteration order consumes a bounded source budget. Capacity and corrupt-record errors still affect the shared source group.
impact: Later routes can wait indefinitely behind persistent earlier backlogs; queue pressure can stop source-wide discovery. Work is retained rather than silently discarded.
evidence: Node interchain/runtime/iln_observer_retry.go:17-25,74-105,141-199 and iln_observer_worker.go:128-162,180-210. A bounded scheduler check reproduced lack of service to a later route; existing durability tests passed.
remediation: Rotate retry service fairly, quarantine corruption without losing original evidence, expose backlog age/capacity, and verify a healthy late route progresses under sustained earlier failures.
limits: The current small route set was not observed stalled. The starvation scenario exercises a larger/backlogged scheduler; no disk power-loss or production outage test.

title: External source witnesses retain correlated-provider trust
condition: External signing requires two differently labelled operators with complete matching evidence. The first matching pair wins; an earlier disagreement is not a global veto, and labels cannot prove independent upstream infrastructure.
impact: Two colluding or correlated data sources can give honest validators a consistent false view. Multiple BLS keys do not remove that shared evidence dependency. One faulty independently counted witness alone is insufficient; a physical upstream can nevertheless correlate more than one label. Duplicated URLs with the same label do not add votes.
evidence: Node config.go, evm/rpc_evidence_quorum.go and tests, evm/finality.go and tests, runtime/iln_direct_signing.go. Existing and bounded injected-reader checks; live reachability of configured endpoints; primary provider/finality documentation.
remediation: Record actual provider and fallback-pair independence, monitor disagreements, preserve fail-closed per-witness checks and explicitly accept the L2 safe model. Reassess if operational evidence shows two counted operators share a controlling upstream.
limits: Medium is a current residual architecture assessment, not a claim of independent upstream attestation or formal risk acceptance. Correlated fabricated real RPC receipts and a live authorization based on fabricated source evidence were not constructed. This is not a claimed cryptographic BLS break.

title: Quote-writer readiness misses required SQL privileges
condition: Current restricted-role migrations omit SELECT on xita_transfer_operations, although the aggregate quote-capacity query now joins it. The readiness query does not test this dependency.
impact: A deployment using the documented dedicated quote writer can advertise readiness while every quote promising at least one positive sponsor grant fails. The transaction rolls back; this is availability failure, not an unsigned or partially journaled promise.
evidence: Managed-relay tax-evidence.mjs:130-145, server.mjs:92-101, SQL migrations010/011. Exact migrations and real saveQuoteEvidence under PostgreSQL/WASM reproduced readiness true then error42501 and zero committed evidence rows.
remediation: Grant only required reads through reviewed migrations; readiness must exercise the complete restricted-role operation or validate every dependency, including resolution evidence.
limits: A consolidated installed writer may already have permission. Production database roles were not accessible; live sponsorship unavailability is not attributed to this defect without host evidence.

title: Sponsor reservation can strand the sender nonce after interruption
condition: The grant reservation commits before signed transaction bytes or a durable hash exist. Reconciliation covers submitted rows with hashes, leaving pre-broadcast or uncertain reserved states without a complete recovery path.
impact: An interrupted grant can retain the unique sponsor nonce and block later grants while the chain pending nonce remains unchanged. It also remains an outstanding financial promise.
evidence: Managed-relay gas-sponsor.mjs:209-223,340-343. Exported-function fault injection and actual PostgreSQL reservation/uniqueness/reconciliation checks reproduced the wedge.
remediation: Durably journal exact signed transaction bytes and expected hash before broadcast; reconcile all lifecycle states, safely rebroadcast the same bytes and resolve uncertain outcomes without duplicate payment.
limits: No live process crash or real sponsor transfer was induced. The current uniqueness guard prevents conflicting nonce reuse; do not remove it as a shortcut.

title: One grant RPC failure can block all-chain sponsorship
condition: One pending grant receipt error escapes the reconciliation loop, which is awaited before any new candidates. Oldest-only bounded windows also lack robust fairness.
impact: An outage on one chain can stop healthy-chain payouts and delay owed grants. This is broader than an individual provider timeout.
evidence: Managed-relay gas-sponsor.mjs:340-361,475-476. Offline injected503 on the first chain prevented examination of a healthy subsequent chain.
remediation: Isolate failures per grant and chain, bound work, apply backoff and rotate scheduling while retaining ambiguous liabilities. Demonstrate healthy-chain progress during another chain outage.
limits: No production worker outage was generated; the live endpoint reports unavailable sponsorship but does not identify its cause.

title: Mailbox completion can conceal a pending native-principal claim
condition: A valid native delivery that cannot pay the recipient within the router gas allowance records a backed pending claim and returns success. The UI equates Mailbox delivery with completed native payout and exposes no claim workflow.
impact: The wallet can show completion while its native balance remains unchanged. A smart wallet able to call the claim method can redirect payout; an arbitrary contract without such an execution path cannot be assumed recoverable.
evidence: XETAGuardedNativeWarpRouter.sol:25-38,68-85; transfer-status-flow.js:119-145; transfer-token-journey.js. Real Mailbox/router integration with explicitly mocked authentication reproduced backed pending funds; actual UI projection reproduced the misleading completion.
remediation: Index deferred delivery, show the claim balance separately, add beneficiary-authorized claim/recovery instructions and verify supported smart-wallet execution. Until then restrict supported native recipients and describe this limit accurately.
limits: No BLS bypass or unbacked claim. The test uses mocked ISM only to isolate the delivery boundary; separate real EIP-2537 vectors passed.

title: Authorized ownership transfer can collapse service/admin separation
condition: Constructor and service-wallet rotation checks enforce distinct roles, but inherited two-step ownership transfer can nominate and accept the current service wallet.
impact: An authorized administrator can accidentally defeat the intended independent recovery authority. No unprivileged privilege escalation or principal sweep is present.
evidence: XITAExecutionGateway.sol:130-155 and inherited ownership transitions; local two-step transition reproduced. Live roles are distinct on all three chains.
remediation: Enforce inequality at ownership nomination, acceptance and setServiceWallet, including pendingOwner. Recheck current roles at acceptance to cover both transition orders; retain independent recovery key custody.
limits: Requires authorized owner action; current deployments do not exhibit collapsed roles.

title: Membership authorizations omit the exact registry deployment
condition: Membership payloads bind chain/domain, set, action, expiry and keys but not the registry address. Matching parallel deployments can accept the same valid transition.
impact: Cross-instance membership replay is possible during overlapping equivalent deployments. Transfer authorizations separately bind the destination ISM and registry, so this is not a transfer-message replay.
evidence: XGRInterchainValidatorRegistryV3.sol:376-460 and XITADirectProtocol.sol:42-49. An explicitly mocked verifier isolated the identical payload/state-machine behavior; current manifests pin one registry per chain.
remediation: Maintain the documented single-active-registry invariant. Reopen protocol domain design before overlapping migration or parallel registries; bind deployment identity in a deliberately versioned membership scheme if that invariant changes.
limits: ACCEPTED_RISK refers to the pre-existing documented architectural decision, limited to its stated controls. No new blanket operator acceptance is invented. The audit cannot prove no unlisted parallel contract exists.

title: Minimum validator committee size remains an operating rule
condition: The registry accepts a nonempty bootstrap and allows authorized reductions to one member; the correctly computed two-thirds quorum then becomes one signature.
impact: An authorized configuration can reduce fault tolerance below the intended launch committee. This is a governance/operations condition, not an unprivileged quorum bypass.
evidence: contracts/XGRInterchainValidatorRegistryV3.sol:122-135,306-335,630-631; isolated policy tests with mocked cryptography. All three observed registries have three members and threshold two, with identical ordered keys.
remediation: Monitor at least three independently operated active members and concentration, and verify current-set re-attestation continuity. Consider a protocol minimum only with an explicit governance/migration design.
limits: Separate physical operators and retained key custody were not independently attested. A permanent loss of quorum has no administrator bypass.

title: Wallet proof calldata is not fully bound to selected intent
condition: The browser and indexer validate metadata, destination, selector and zero value but do not independently hash the actual process message bytes against the selected transfer.
impact: A compromised response may cause gas expenditure on another independently valid message. The destination still enforces cryptographic authentication; no forged mint or principal redirection is established.
evidence: apps/web/transfer-actions.js:614-674; services/indexer/transfer-recovery.mjs:65-87; honest native-relayer construction separately binds the complete payload.
remediation: Decode and bind the actual authorization and message before wallet submission, including destination and selected message ID.
limits: Static defense-in-depth finding; no malicious browser/mainnet transaction executed.

title: Regression fixtures and CI discovery drift from the current product
condition: A Solidity expected-revert is misplaced; old checker hook/chain assumptions and several UI/indexer assertions no longer match current behavior. Selected CI lists omit some discovered tests.
impact: A passing selected pipeline does not establish a clean full regression baseline. The observed failures do not themselves demonstrate a factory bypass or incorrect current token mapping.
evidence: Unmodified Solidity102/103, UI273/280 (five stale assertions and two missing-browser failures), indexer136/137. Corrected isolated factory setup passes. Existing compatibility checker conditions were statically inspected.
remediation: Repair expectations against current deployment/catalog facts, make test discovery explicit and run supported browser/wallet acceptance checks. Keep failed originals visible in evidence.
limits: Two browser checks were not executable because Chromium was unavailable. Do not count them as product regressions or successful browser tests.

title: Production sponsorship and installation readiness remain unproven
condition: Live managed health reports sponsorship enabled but unavailable on all three chains. One public node reports a current version and healthy observer, but host-level binary/service/database attestations are absent.
impact: A publicly advertised sponsored low-gas experience is not currently demonstrated operational. Self-funded users and authenticated principal recovery are separate paths; source fixes alone do not attest installation.
evidence: Read-only live/observations.json and route-configuration.json; downloaded release digest and embedded source revision; current app.js/catalog exact hashes.
remediation: Restore and verify sponsored-service readiness or explicitly restrict the service to self-funded users. Obtain installed binary hashes, service revisions, restricted-role checks and real representative one-/two-hop acceptance evidence.
limits: No specific source defect is asserted as the cause of live unavailability. F-01 remains an independent P0; disabling sponsorship cannot resolve it.

title: Expiry-release evidence trusts one RPC without a canonical reread
condition: Expired unused quote capacity is released after chain-native finality-qualified nonce inspection through one configured provider, pinned by block number without a final canonical hash reread. Base/Arbitrum use finalized; XGR uses latest under the adopted committed-IBFT model.
impact: A false or inconsistent source view can remove a real pending commitment from liability accounting and allow overcommitment of optional sponsor treasury.
evidence: gas-sponsor.mjs:87-98,399-430 and tax-evidence.mjs:130-137; the exported expiry function accepted one head read and a numeric nonce read in an isolated check. The five-minute grace and native finality head are real mitigations.
remediation: Use complete canonical finalized evidence with post-read hash verification and an explicitly justified provider trust policy; retain ambiguous paid liabilities until safely resolved.
limits: This does not grant Direct-BLS signing or access user principal. No real false provider or production insolvency was induced.

title: Unpaid quote reservations can still occupy sponsorship capacity
condition: Unauthenticated clients can reserve real sponsorship capacity with signed public quotes. Expiry reconciliation and rate limits shorten the window but do not prove wallet control or prevent repeated distributed occupation.
impact: Legitimate users requesting new sponsored quotes can encounter unavailable capacity despite no attacker payment. This concerns quote admission, not proof that already paid grants are directly displaced by unpaid quotes. Limits and reconciliation mitigate occupation but do not establish a maximum holding time.
evidence: Current quote rate limits, aggregate admission SQL, 90-second lifetime and five-minute post-expiry reconciliation reviewed; historical N-06 original long-lived daily occupation is materially reduced.
remediation: Distinguish provisional quote reservations from paid obligations, preserve safe accounting and add fair admission/abuse controls justified by measured service demand. Do not release ambiguous paid promises merely to regain capacity.
limits: No distributed production denial-of-service test. Five minutes is an eligibility grace, not a guaranteed release deadline: finalized-head delay, RPC failure and bounded oldest-first processing can extend reservation indefinitely.

title: Conservative daily-limit accounting can count a liability twice
condition: Matching reserved, submitted and needs-review grants created within the rolling24-hour window contribute both to daily spent accounting and to still-open commitment accounting.
impact: The same in-flight obligation can conservatively consume capacity twice, reducing availability. The demonstrated direction is under-admission, not unbacked payment.
evidence: tax-evidence.mjs:130-160 and sponsor-funding.mjs:42-52; static SQL/arithmetic review, not a separately executed database double-count test.
remediation: Define mutually exclusive economic states and reconcile daily spend with outstanding liabilities using one documented accounting model, retaining conservative treatment of uncertain outcomes.
limits: No production utilization calculation was inspected; no solvency violation is claimed from this observation alone.

title: Paid grant lifecycle can remain unresolved after early delivery or shutdown
condition: An unpaid upfront grant can become ineligible once an external valid delivery advances the transfer. Disabling sponsorship also stops processing while existing obligations remain.
impact: Immutable paid promises can remain neither fulfilled nor safely resolved, occupying liability capacity and stranding the promised gas experience. Principal delivery may itself have succeeded.
evidence: gas-sponsor.mjs:27-38,100-116,429-470 and server.mjs:401-427; stage eligibility and disabled-worker paths reviewed. Current UI gates normal progression on grants, but permissionless external delivery is an independent path.
remediation: Specify and implement durable obligation resolution across externally advanced transfers and service shutdown. Separate stopping new promises from draining or explicitly settling existing paid obligations.
limits: No production unpaid-promise inventory was accessible. An operator switch is authorized behavior; the issue is the missing complete lifecycle for prior commitments.

title: Pending recovery work can be removed before durable replacement
condition: Set rotation or missing route handling can remove an old durable vote before replacement signing succeeds. Age-based cleanup also relies on assumed regeneration without a durable successor job.
impact: A restart/rotation or temporary verification failure can lose automatic recovery work. A known source hash and available current quorum may still allow manual recovery.
evidence: Node interchain/runtime/iln_checkpoint.go:383-400 and iln_storage.go:80-85; current static control-flow reassessment against the retrieved historical condition.
remediation: Retain original recovery evidence until a durable replacement or terminal authenticated delivery exists; journal transitions atomically and test restart/rotation failure boundaries.
limits: No destructive restart/rotation experiment was performed. This was identified during Phase B and was not retroactively added to the frozen Phase A.

title: Successful incomplete discovery responses can advance durable cursors
condition: Discovery accepts the first successful single-provider log set; an incomplete but well-formed response can still be followed by cursor persistence.
impact: Real operations or route notices can be missed by automatic discovery. Later signing still requires complete two-operator evidence; omission affects availability, not forged authorization.
evidence: Node evm multi-Gateway scanner and runtime/iln_observer_worker.go:150-153; RouteAdded discovery has the same completeness trust boundary.
remediation: Add independent completeness checks, safe overlap/reconciliation or authenticated log-range mechanisms; preserve known-transaction recovery and alert on inconsistent sources.
limits: A valid empty response cannot be declared false from syntax alone. No actual provider censorship or production missing transfer was demonstrated.

title: Admin deployment evidence uses confirmation depth as finality
condition: The deployment verifier can label confirmation-depth-qualified receipts as finalized without requiring the adopted native safe/IBFT policy.
impact: A future deployment could be promoted on weaker evidence than its label promises. Current read-only canonical runtime checks provide separate assurance for the observed deployed contracts.
evidence: services/admin/deployment-ledger.mjs:107-167; actual current verifier reproduced the historical acceptance boundary, recorded in evidence/contracts/admin-reassessment.json.
remediation: Apply shared chain-native finality and canonical receipt verification before deployment promotion; represent provisional depth separately from native finality.
limits: No new deployment or real reorganization. Repair is required before a future deployment/promotion, even though this audit authorizes documentation only.

title: Orphaned deployment locks require careful manual recovery
condition: A process interruption can leave a file lock whose existence blocks later journal mutation even after a new process opens the intact journal.
impact: Administrator deployment recovery can stop until the stale owner is safely established and the lock resolved. This does not itself cause duplicate broadcast or loss of the recorded intent.
evidence: services/admin/deployment-intents.mjs:96-117,203-214; actual functions reproduced the stale-lock condition in an isolated directory (evidence/contracts/admin-reassessment.json).
remediation: Use robust process ownership or leases and a documented stale-lock recovery procedure that preserves journal and signed transaction identity. Time expiry alone must not evict a live writer.
limits: No production journal was inspected or changed.

title: Fee-tax backfill omits required verified event identity
condition: backfillPaidFeeTax builds an event without messageId and txHash although storeVerifiedOperation requires both, even after successful upstream verification.
impact: Eligible fee-evidence rows remain held and repeated sweeps roll back instead of completing reconciliation. Primary new ingestion is separate.
evidence: services/indexer/transfer-index-worker.mjs:54-61,494-524; relocated historical local check against current functions reproduced verified0/held1 with BEGIN/ROLLBACK and no insert.
remediation: Carry the already verified row identities into the common store call; distinguish guard defects from temporarily missing evidence and add a successful-store regression.
limits: No principal access or unauthorized payout; production tax records were not read.

title: Dense event windows lack adaptive progress
condition: Oversized route or grouped-source log windows are rejected and retried with the same range; increasing the shared cap does not provide adaptive splitting.
impact: Legitimate dense history can stall automatic indexing. Manual known-hash recovery and announcements remain separate mitigations.
evidence: Current transfer-index.mjs size guards and worker loops; two new isolated boundary tests reproduced unchanged windows. See evidence/indexer/historical-checks.tap.
remediation: Adaptively split block windows and fully process a single dense block under bounded resource control. Never truncate logs silently.
limits: The new tests intentionally exercise the early size boundary, not full canonical validation of hundreds of real transfers. No live dense window was established.

title: Unknown route rows can starve background delivery refresh
condition: The background SQL limit is applied before resolving active routes; unknown rows skip both checking and scheduling timestamp advancement.
impact: A sufficient old retired backlog can indefinitely hide healthy active-route delivery work. The wallet API sorting fix does not correct the background worker.
evidence: transfer-index-worker.mjs:197-225; PR310 explicitly has partial scope and changes transfer-index-store.mjs only. Actual current migrations and PostgreSQL/WASM selection reproduced two sweeps with no active-route read.
remediation: Filter or schedule against active route identity before limiting, rotate/quarantine unknown work without losing history, and test background progress with a large retired backlog.
limits: The production database backlog was not inspected; live eight-route coverage is a snapshot, not this adversarial acceptance test.

title: Published CLI version fields are empty despite valid embedded VCS data
condition: The release workflow targets an obsolete versioning package path, so product Release version, Git branch, Commit hash and Build time fields remain empty.
impact: Operational self-reporting is weaker and can confuse rollout checks. Independent download hashes and embedded Go VCS metadata still identify the published source revision.
evidence: The downloaded v3.3.8 binary version command exited0 and returned all four fields as <none>; go version -m reports the exact frozen revision and vcs.modified=false.
remediation: Fix linker targets and require nonempty expected CLI fields plus matching embedded VCS revision in release gates; attest actual installed file hashes separately.
limits: No daemon was launched; RPC self-reported version is not a disk-hash attestation. No signing or access-control failure is implied.

title: Compiler advisory applicability remains an assurance gap
condition: Solidity0.8.24 with viaIR/Yul optimization lies within the affected configuration range of SOL-2026-7. Project-specific trigger/alias conditions have not been conclusively excluded.
impact: Potential compiler exposure remains open as an assurance task, without a demonstrated XITA miscompilation or established principal-loss path.
evidence: Official Solidity known-bugs advisory, foundry.toml settings and independent runtime/body comparison. Existing cryptographic and accounting tests are useful but not a compiler differential proof.
remediation: For existing artifacts compare the exact solc0.8.24 build/settings with the targeted fix applied, or obtain a suitable equivalence proof. Source/IR review or an arbitrary newer compiler build alone is not definitive. Qualify a fixed compiler separately for future builds; investigate concrete differences before deciding on existing deployments.
limits: No claim that all deployed contracts are exploitable; no broad redeployment is recommended solely from the advisory.

title: Membership and governance submission RPC remains unbounded
condition: The read-side witness transport has deadlines and cancellation, but membership and governance submission paths construct a separate transaction relayer without the bounded client or worker shutdown context. Its receipt timeout setting controls polling intervals rather than individual I/O deadlines.
impact: A hanging submission or preflight call can retain a worker indefinitely and block orderly shutdown. Shared source locks and outer polling add further lifecycle pressure; fixing ordinary read-side RPC does not close the whole original boundary.
evidence: Node interchain/evm/client.go:400-448, interchain/evm/iln_governance_submit.go:130-153 and txrelayer/txrelayer.go:61-80,256-275; governance execution and membership submission are active callers. Static source/dependency tracing confirms the unbounded transport; existing transport cancellation tests exercise the bounded read client only.
remediation: Propagate bounded context-aware clients through every preflight, send and receipt wait; define transaction-uncertainty recovery and verify complete Worker.Close termination. Do not merely add an outer sleep timeout or automatically rebroadcast a different transaction.
limits: No new transaction or hanging submission was executed. This Phase-B finding supersedes an initially considered Low classification for bounded shutdown delays; the final assessment is Medium/P1 OPEN.
